## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")
library("naniar")
library("readxl")
```

```{r cars}
alc <- read_excel("AlcoholAttrDeaths.xlsx") %>% clean_names()
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

Mutate to add a "CA" column, slice sections, and join

```{r}
glimpse(alc2)
summary(alc2) #NA=-,x,NA
```


```{r}
alc %>%
  select(-x2) %>% 
  rename("Effect"=annual_average_for_california_2020_2021,
         "Male"=x3,
         "Female"=x4) %>%
  slice(13:25,28:36,39:43,46:52,55:60,65:66,69,72,76:88) %>% 
  mutate(State="CA",
            Effect_Duration = case_when(
            row_number() %in% c(1:40) ~ "Chronic",
            row_number() %in% c(41:57) ~ "Acute",
            TRUE ~ NA_character_),
          Effect_Category = case_when(
            row_number() %in% c(1:13) ~ "100% Alcohol-Attributable",
            row_number() %in% c(14:22) ~ "Cancer",
            row_number() %in% c(23:27) ~ "Heart Disease and Stroke",
            row_number() %in% c(28:34) ~ "Liver, Gallbladder, and Pancreas",
            row_number() %in% c(35:40) ~ "Other Chronic Causes",
            row_number() %in% c(41:42) ~ "Alcohol-Related Poisonings",
            row_number() %in% c(43) ~ "Motor Vehicle Traffic Crashes",
            row_number() %in% c(44) ~ "Suicide",
            row_number() %in% c(45:57) ~ "Other Acute Causes",
            TRUE ~ NA_character_),
         across(everything(), ~if_else(.=="x",NA,.)),
         across(c(Male, Female), as.numeric),        
         across(everything(), ~replace_na(., 0)),
         Male = if_else(row_number() == 14, NA, Male),
         Female = if_else(row_number() == 21, NA, Female)) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Male, Female),
               names_to = "Gender",
               values_to = "Deaths") %>% 
  select(State, Effect_Duration, Effect_Category, Gender, Effect, Deaths)

```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
